independent_reasoning.P1: For closed S, scale each Liouville equality along an actual current-topology Thurston sequence, use bilinear continuity, and obtain equality against all measured laminations. Positivity not needed for this implication but is required elsewhere. Replacing all Liouville tests by these boundary tests fails by Leininger explicit filling-curve construction, whose simple arc intersection values agree but homology classes differ up to sign.
independent_reasoning.P2: For essential simple alpha on closed genus>=2 S, each cut component has genus>=1. A relative filling system can be chosen avoiding alpha. Each zero intersection removes transverse crossings of supported geodesics by positive local-box mass. Every remaining complete geodesic lies in a lifted disk (impossible), compact annulus lift (bounded neighborhood of alpha-axis, thus same endpoints), or selected curve (excluded by a selected dual). Invariance on discrete alpha-lift orbit supplies b alpha; one positive metric length determines b.
independent_reasoning.P3: Liouville full support satisfies Bonahon Proposition 4 crossing condition; fixed positive length lies in a compact bounded-intersection slice. Each all-metric equality is closed affine; fiber contains gamma, hence nonempty compact convex. No extreme-point or finite-support conclusion follows.
independent_reasoning.P4: Under the explicitly stated finite-area cusped convention only, Teich of S_0,3 is one point. Liouville endpoint-pair density is locally finite off diagonal and non-atomic. Bonahon local flow-box length calculation extends to this finite-area quotient and gives i(L,L)=pi^2|chi|=pi^2, since volume(PT S)=pi area(S), measure=volume/2. Positive scaling to length of AB works. AB trace6 is hyperbolic and nonperipheral. Nonzero scaled nonatomic measure cannot equal a finite sum of atomic counting currents. The result is not asserted under compact-core currents, variable-boundary metrics, or every possible complete infinite-area metric.
independent_reasoning.source_conventions: K3 p84 resolves the initial seal uncertainty: oriented finite type by default, boundary/punctures allowed. p96 says complete hyperbolic metrics, but does not itself explicitly restrict to finite area. Therefore the fixed finite-area interpretation is a labeled supplementary convention, not a proof of the unqualified question across every metric convention.
